newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - May 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - May 19.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Essendon veteran Michael Long is today considering whether to take action against after an alleged racial incident in yesterday's game against St Kilda. Long was the catalyst for the AFL's strong anti-racial laws, after a successful action against Collinwood player Damian Monkhorst two years ago. Page 19.

The ACT Brumbies has won the chance to host a semi-final at their home ground in Canberra next week, with a 35-29 win against the Wellington Hurricanes in New Zealand yesterday. Running with a strong breeze in the first half, the Brumbies held off a lastminute surge by Wellington to secure second place on the Super 12 table. Page 21.

The Fremantle Dockers clinched a dramatic, last minute win against the struggling Brisbane Lions in their Australian Football match yesterday after Fremantle forward Quenton Leach booted a goal after the siren, angering Lions' coach John Northey, who feltLeach had pushed Brisbane fullback Shane Clayton. Page 22.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Western Suburbs won 32-12 in a tough and physical encounter against the South Queensland Crushers yesterday. Captain and playmaker Paul Langmack was instrumental in the win, despite early fears he would miss the match after being knocked out following a lash of heads in the first minute. Page 22.

North Sydney clinched a dramatic 19-18 win against Sydney City yesterday, after Bear's half back Jason Taylor potted a field goal with two minutes remaining. The kick came only minutes after Taylor made a woeful attempt to convert a David Fairleigh try, kick which Taylor described as one of his worst. Page 22.

Sydney United booked itself a place in next week's grand final against the Brisbane Strikers after a 1-0 victory against South Melbourne yesterday, thanks to a volley from Ante Milicic midway through the second half. The game was marred by violence afterthe game, when opposing supporters clashed with police on the field of Parramatta Stadium. Page 27.
THE AGE

The Australian women's basketball team continued its unbeaten run against the Russian team in their five match series with a 77-73 victory in Bendigo last night. Rachel Sporn and Trish Fallon were the best for the Opals, finishing with 16 and 15 points rspectively. The series concludes tonight in Melbourne.

Trainer Len Smith has announced Darren Gauci will ride Skybeau in today's Adelaide Cup, after original rider Jason Holder suffered a broken arm in a fall during Saturday's SAJC Oaks. Skybeau, last year's third place getter in the Melbourne Cup, is rated 5/2 chance to take out his home town Cup at Morphetville today.

Classy Melbourne Magic player Sam Mackinnon scored a game-high 32 points and grabbed seven rebounds to secure a win against the Perth Wildcats in their National Basketball League match on Saturday. Magic coach Brian Goorjian praised the effort of Macinno, saying the Boomers player is benefiting from increased confidence.
THE HERALD SUN

The playing future of Hawthorn's goal kicking legend Jason Dunstall is under serious threat, after he succumbed to a knee injury in yesterday's match against Carlton. Dunstall, who is only 100 goals short of the all-time goal kicking record, will today b examined by an orthopaedic surgeon to determine if the star full-forward will ever play again. Page 96.

Adelaide Crows coach Malcolm Blight has hit out at the tactics used by the Sydney Swans after the Crow's comprehensive win on Saturday night. Blight said the Swan's flooding of the defence slows down the game, and threatens the entertainment value of AFL football. Page 93.

The New South Wales Waratahs rediscovered its attacking flair in a courageous 34-20 loss to Super 12 champions Auckland. The Blues held an encouraging 20-13 lead at half time, but could not stop a fast finishing Auckland team, which leaves the Blues in ninth position, just ahead of Queensland on percentages. Page 87.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Australian cricket selectors have rested opening batsman Michael Slater for the team's one day cricket match against Tom Moody's Worcestershire. Adam Gilchrist has forced his way back into the side, batting at number six, so too have Michael Bevan and Grg Blewitt who have both been recovering from injury. Page 31.

The ARL will today launch an inquiry into allegations that North Sydney and Sydney City trainers were involved in on-field training in yesterday's match. Referee Paul Simpkins stopped the game four minutes from full time to send Norths' trainer Steve Hanon and City's Ron Palmer from the field. Page 32.

Manly has reversed its spate of poor performances in recent weeks with a 30 to 16 win against South Sydney yesterday. Fulton told reporters after the game he agreed with speculation in the past few days that there appears to be a compromise between the ARL and Super League, saying that the division is hurting the game. Page 38.
